text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a pattern where the telemetry re-publisher jobs are hitting route quota and then falling back to the low-concurrency lane. That makes recompute aggregates run at half batch size and we get intermittent OOMs. Anyone else noticing this?

sam: Yep. Observed it last night for the eu-agg job. Error spikes align with route throttles.

priya: Are these the re-publisher -> operator API calls or replayer tasks?

maya: Re-publisher -> internal API (republish.v1.publish). It includes a routing hint header we set in the shim.

sam: I dug in — the shim sets `X-RDWD-Route: replay` by default. Our routing policy maps `replay` to the latency-sensitive lane (low concurrency) because historical replay used to be latency-critical for some storefront flows. This was never updated when we moved large recomputes to the re-publisher pipeline.

eli: That explains the smaller batches. If the route is low-concurrency, the runtime's batching window/slot size is smaller.

maya: Example payload for the republish call for context:
```json
{
  "job_id": "jp-2025-09-13-42",
  "model": "agg-summarizer-v3",
  "route": "replay",
  "batch_hint": 64
}
```

priya: Quick ideas: 1) update shim to set `route: backfill` for re-publisher jobs, 2) add a route-override toggle at job creation in Console, 3) add dashboard annotation + metric to catch route-induced throttles.

sam: +1 to all three. We should be careful: flipping to `backfill` will route to high-throughput GPUs; need to ensure capacity/quota for Dedicated tenants. Might need a soft quota check.

eli: For safe rollout: change shim default to `backfill` only for jobs > 1M events or explicit `--bulk` flag. And push a canary that marks the job metadata so console can show "route_hint: backfill (canaried)".

maya: Console UX ask: add a small field on the re-publish job page: "Desired route (auto)" with options `auto / backfill / replay`. Default auto keeps current behavior. When set to backfill, the backend attaches `X-RDWD-Route: backfill` and shows a warning if tenant quota might be exceeded.

priya: For telemetry/dashboards: add a metric `republisher.route_fallback_count` and a panel that correlates fallback_count, batch_size, and OOM rate. Also emit an event when a job is downgraded to low-concurrency.

sam: API change is tiny — header or body hint. But the routing switch touches the quota calculator. I can add a check in the coordinator that simulates the route selection and returns `quota_ok: boolean` in the job create response. That gives Console a chance to warn.

eli: Also add a short-lived feature flag `republish-route-default-backfill` so we can flip for prod after canary.

maya: Action items:
- sam: implement coordinator quota-sim endpoint (+1 week)
- priya: add dashboard panels + alert (PR to grafana repo) (+3 days)
- sam: update shim to honor `--bulk` flag and add `route_hint` metadata (PR + tests) (+4 days)
- maya: Console wireframe for route override + warning (I'll drop Figma link) (+2 days)

priya: Will also create a lightweight postmortem draft with impact numbers once we have the route_fallback_count.

deploy-bot: sam pushed 2 commits to branch `republisher/route-hint` (link: https://git.company/republisher/compare).

sam: starting with a canary deploy to staging. Will post results and a sample job id.

maya: Thanks — let's aim to have the canary metrics in Grafana within 48h and then roll to prod behind the feature flag. :thumbsup:

eli: noted. If we see any tenant quota contention, we'll auto-revert the default.

maya: closing loop — big win if this reduces OOMs and avoids unnecessary recompute retries.

sam: sounds good, thanks all.
